title: C# 8 to C# 14 feature map (cross-module synthesis)
hook: C# 8 through C# 14 added nullable reference types, records, pattern matching, async streams, collection expressions, and more — spread across the modules you already studied. This topic maps each version to where you learned it and what interviewers still ask.

blocks.text: Language versions are not random feature dumps — they build on earlier modules. C# 8 brought nullable reference types (module 07), ranges, and async streams (module 13). C# 9 brought records and init (modules 04–05). C# 10 brought file-scoped namespaces and global usings (module 01). C# 11 added raw strings and required members. C# 12 collection expressions (module 08). C# 13 params collections. C# 14 refactors field-backed properties and span conversions (modules 04, 17).

blocks.text: Senior interviews ask you to name C# 9 versus 11 features in context — not recite a changelog. Mapping features to modules shows you used them in production: records for DTOs, pattern matching for auth branching (module 11), IAsyncEnumerable for paging (module 13), Span for parsing (module 17).

blocks.title: Study method
blocks.body: For each version, recall one module topic and one real scenario — SQS consumer, Redis cache, CSV import.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Listing features without tying to a module or use case. Assuming latest LangVersion on an old Target Framework Moniker (TFM) — syntax may compile but APIs may not exist. Confusing C# version with .NET runtime version.

interviewTakeaways: Map C# 8–14 features to modules you studied — records, NRT, patterns, spans.
LangVersion is syntax; TFM is available APIs.
Interviewers want scenarios, not changelog recitation.
commonPitfalls: LangVersion 14 on netstandard2.0 with missing APIs.
Ignoring which features need nullable context enabled.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS strictness and ECMAScript yearly releases mirror C# LangVersion plus TFM — two axes, not one.
